Pell.narrative: I was bound to Josiah Crane's foundry at fourteen and learned fire there — how to read a bloom, how to keep a tuyere from slagging, how a bellows breathes. A month before my indenture was out I walked off the poor terrace and kept walking until the woods took me in. Kai found me on the stone road half-starved and brought me to Coldwell, and here I am: an outlaw with a foundry in his hands and no paper to prove he was ever anything else. There is a letter sewn in my coat that I have not shown anyone, not even Kai.
values: keeping my own fire and my own name
paying back the people who took me in
never being owned by a contract again
goals: stay out of Crane's reach until the indenture is forgotten
make myself useful enough at Coldwell that nobody asks where I came from
learn to fight properly from Kai
build a small forge of his own at Coldwell, hidden from the road, and remember his hands are his
learn to fight properly from Kai until he can stand his ground without a hammer

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He pulled me off the road and never once asked what I was running from. I would stand beside him against anything.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: leader
relations.note: She took me in when she had no reason to. I keep her fire and her tools and I do not make her regret it.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: household
relations.note: He is loud and rough on the road, but he is the one who taught me which end of a stave to hold.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: household
relations.note: She slips me an extra bowl when the pot is thin and never says a word about it.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: He knows the woods like a priest knows his prayers. I go out with him for wood and keep my mouth shut.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: elder
relations.note: He talks about the old garden patch and the Lean Year and I listen. He does not ask me about Kettlebridge.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: old master
relations.note: He owns my years on paper. Every time I hear a cart on the stone road I think it is him come to collect.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: The Council's scribe writes the indentures. If anyone can read me back into that foundry it is him.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: the boy
relations.note: He is small and still coughs from the winter. I keep the fire high for him.

memories.gist: The day I walked off the poor terrace with my apron still on and my hands black to the wrist, and did not look back at the works chimneys.
Kai finding me on the stone road, giving me half a loaf and saying Coldwell had room for one more.
Marta putting a mallet and a pair of tongs in my hands and telling me to keep the common fire banked through the night.
The night the letter came up the road and I read the seal by the fire and put it in my coat and said nothing.
Learning at the foundry to judge a bloom by its colour — cherry, then straw, then grey — and being proud of it.

stances.why: A written indenture made me a thing that could be fetched back; I would rather live in the woods on roots than sign another.
The common fire is the one thing I am trusted with here, and a cold hearth would send me back out on the road.
He is the only person since the foundry who wanted me for nothing.
If Marta knew Crane's people were asking after me she might send me on for the household's sake, and I have nowhere else.

Pell.secret: The letter from Barnaby Quill asking after him on the Coldwell road is sewn into his coat; he has told no one, not Kai, and the indenture paper is folded inside it.
pastimes: banking the common fire at Coldwell so it burns even and clean through the night
mending pots and hinges for the household with a hand-bellows he rigged from a hide and two boards
walking the stone road at dusk to watch the Kettlebridge carts and guess what each load weighs
Pell.calling: I read fire for a living — give me a bloom and a bellows and I'll tell you what the iron means to be.

Hob Ferrier.narrative: I hunted these woods for the steading before the Lean Year, and I hunt them still — only now the meat goes into a common pot that is not mine, in a house that is not mine, on land that was. The Tolleys sleep in the barn I raised, and the Guild counts rent off my father's fields. I walk the edge of those fields so Hal Tolley can see me do it. Marta says keep off the tenants; I have kept off them so far.
values: my own hands and my own bow
not being made a beggar on my own ground
goals: see the Tolleys off the Coldwell fields one way or another
keep the household in meat through the winter
get a pardon, or a field, or at least a reckoning
keep the household in meat through the winter, whatever else comes
get a pardon, or a field, or at least a reckoning before he's too old to draw a bow

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: leader
relations.note: She has held us together since the fields went. I mind her word — mostly.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: hunting partner
relations.note: We hunt together and we think alike about the Tolleys. He is the only one who does not preach at me.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: A quay man, but he can fight and he does not flinch. I would take him into the woods any day.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: A foundry boy with soft hands. He is learning the woods slow, but he carries a load without complaining.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: household
relations.note: She cooks what I bring and never asks where the hides go. That is worth something.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: old neighbour
relations.note: He remembers the steading whole, same as me. We do not talk about the Tolleys in front of the young ones.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He sleeps in my barn and calls it his. He will not sleep easy while I am in these woods.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: Her Guild holds the lease on my fields and sends its tenants to farm them. She has never once come out to see what she took.

relations.name: Hedric Ashby
relations.label: accuser
relations.note: He says I stole his hides. His snare line was cut by someone, and it was not me, but he will not hear it.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: He declared us outlaws at the gate over fields he had already taken. I would not piss on him if he were burning.

relations.name: Marta Tolley
relations.label: tenant's wife
relations.note: She keeps the house that was ours and puts a wall up round the yard as if she had built it.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: Hedric's brother
relations.note: Osbert has never said a hard word to my face, but he is Hedric's brother and he farms the meadows that look down on our old fields. He believes what his brother tells him about the hides, I reckon, and he sells grain to the same store that took our barn.

memories.gist: The Lean Year, when the blight took the berries and the Reeve's grain came with a ledger and a price we could not pay.
The day the Guild's men came and read us out of our fields, and the Tolleys walked in behind them with their carts.
Raising the Coldwell barn with my own hands, beam by beam, the year my father died.
Walking the field edge with Ned while Hal Tolley watched us from the barn door, and saying nothing at all.
Selling hides at Ferncross in the dark and being asked no questions, which is how I like it.
Finding Hedric Ashby's snare line cut and empty, and knowing he would put it on me before he had even looked at the ground.

stances.why: My father worked that ground and I raised its barn; no ledger makes it the Guild's.
They took a farm that was already lived in and call themselves tenants. I will not pretend otherwise.
Meat in the pot and hides at Ferncross keep us alive, and the less the road knows of it the better.
She has kept us from being taken so far, and I owe her that, even when her word galls me.
A pardon from the man who outlawed us would be a leash. I would rather be hunted than owned.

pastimes: hunting the woods at first light with Ned, reading sign and setting snares
whittling bow-staves and arrow shafts by the fire while the pot boils
walking the boundary of the old Coldwell fields at dusk so Hal Tolley sees him do it
Hob Ferrier.calling: I'm a hunter — these woods fed my father's table and they'll feed mine, whatever the Guild writes on its paper.
